title: Respect the boundary.
summary: A tenant context follows verified identity and membership.
explanation: The tenant middleware compares the authenticated user’s tenant with the resolved organization before assigning a scoped context. Tenant-aware queries and project policies build on that context.
benefit: Organization membership becomes an explicit precondition for the protected request path.

title: Keep the rules close.
summary: A user story earns its way to completion.
explanation: The UserStory model checks linked work before allowing testing, release, or completion. Completing a story checks that linked tasks and bugs are done and linked test cases have passed.
benefit: A status change reflects the state of the underlying work. The rule lives with the domain model, so the UI cannot be the only place enforcing it.

title: Connect the right people.
summary: Live comments belong to a specific activity.
explanation: Actify routes a comment through its application command, then broadcasts the returned comment to the activity’s SignalR group. Existing comments load for the connecting client.
benefit: A discussion stays attached to its activity, while the client receives live updates without refreshing the page.

title: Commit the whole change.
summary: Related writes share a transaction boundary.
explanation: The Unit of Work runs the use case, saves its changes, and commits. If the operation throws, it rolls the database transaction back. Work-item creation uses this to coordinate its record, project counter, and history.
benefit: Related database updates can succeed or roll back together, keeping the use case’s persistence boundary visible.

title: Ask for the data you need.
summary: A display-name lookup stays a focused projection.
explanation: A dedicated read model filters by work item, project, and tenant, then projects only the code and title. AsNoTracking makes the read intent explicit.
benefit: The caller gets the value it needs without materializing the full work-item domain graph for this lookup.
code:
return await _dbContext.WorkItems
.AsNoTracking()
.Where(workItem =>
    workItem.Id == wId &&
    workItem.ProjectId == pId &&
    workItem.Project.TenantId == tId)
.Select(workItem =>
    workItem.Code + " - " + workItem.Title)
.FirstOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken);

title: Give refresh tokens a lifecycle.
summary: Successful refresh replaces and revokes the old token.
explanation: IdentityService checks the stored token’s active state. A successful refresh records revocation, links the replacement token, and persists the new token with an expiry.
benefit: Refresh credentials have an explicit lifecycle in persistence, with rotation and revocation represented in the model.

title: Make AI output earn trust.
summary: Structured suggestions are parsed and checked.
explanation: Generated work-item fields go through JSON extraction, typed deserialization, normalization, and usability checks. Invalid output feeds a repair prompt, with bounded attempts and fallback suggestions.
benefit: The model’s text passes through application rules before it becomes a usable suggestion. The normal command path still validates the user’s final choice.

title: Record the change that matters.
summary: History captures differences with useful display values.
explanation: The history recorder compares old and new property values, skips unchanged values and ignored technical fields, and resolves related identifiers into display text before recording a change.
benefit: Project history explains what changed in terms a teammate can understand, alongside who made the change.

title: Preserve the meaning of a sprint.
summary: Carry unfinished work forward without losing completed history.
explanation: Completing a sprint moves only incomplete work back to the backlog. Completed items remain associated with that sprint, while the lifecycle update and history are committed together.
benefit: Historical sprint reports can continue to describe the work delivered in that sprint after the remaining scope moves on.
code:
await workItemsRepository
    .MoveIncompleteWorkItemsFromSprintToBacklogAsync(
        tenantId,
        sprint.Id,
        sprint.ProjectId,
        transactionCancellationToken);

sprint.Complete();

title: Make editing intent explicit.
summary: Ignore, clear, and set are different operations.
explanation: PatchHelpers gives string updates three meanings: null leaves the existing value alone, whitespace clears it, and supplied text sets a trimmed value. Work-item updates use these decisions explicitly.
benefit: A partial edit can distinguish an omitted field from a deliberate request to remove its value.

title: Let each response own its job.
summary: Notification handlers keep recipient logic separate.
explanation: Sprint completion publishes a domain-relevant application event. A dedicated handler derives distinct recipients from the team snapshot and creates their notifications; a separate handler owns email delivery.
benefit: The command describes the business change, while each follow-up handler owns its delivery responsibility. These are in-process MediatR events.

title: Schedule work with a lifecycle.
summary: A hosted worker owns the reminder loop and cancellation.
explanation: The event reminder worker uses PeriodicTimer and the host’s stopping token. Each run creates a dependency-injection scope, finds due events, targets attendees, and marks processed reminders.
benefit: Timed work has an explicit owner in the application host. The implementation is an in-process worker, with persistent queueing a possible next step.
